question.problem: According to the rational roots theorem, which of the following could be a root of the polynomial $f(x)=2{x}^{3}+17{x}^{2}-10x-9?$
question.worked_solution:
Given a polynomial with integer coefficients, the rational roots theorem states that any rational roots of the polynomial must take the form

$$
\pm \frac{\text{factor of the constant term}}{\text{factor of the leading coefficient}}.
$$

For the given polynomial $f(x),$ the constant term is $-9,$ and the leading coefficient is $2.$ So, any rational roots of $f(x)$ must take the form

$$
\pm \frac{\text{factor of }-9}{\text{factor of }2}.
$$

Of the given answer choices, only $-\frac{9}{2}$ takes the above form since the numerator $(9)$ is a factor of $-9$ and the denominator $(2)$ is a factor of $2.$
